title: Single-Chain Fab Chain-Exchange (scFab-PACE) converts targeted prodrugs into functional T cell engagers on tumor cells
one_line: The authors describe scFab-PACE, a protein-assembly strategy in which two inactive single-chain Fab prodrug modules exchange chains on the tumor cell surface to assemble an active T cell engager only where the target antigen is present.
key_claims: Individual scFab prodrug components are functionally inert until chain exchange occurs, providing a conditional activation mechanism for T cell engagers.
Chain exchange is driven by co-localization on antigen-positive tumor cells, so assembly of the bispecific engager is target-dependent.
The assembled product engages CD3 and mediates T cell-dependent killing of tumor cells in vitro, whereas the separate prodrug components do not.
Selectivity for antigen-positive over antigen-negative cells is presented as the key advantage of the split-prodrug format over conventional T cell engagers.
limitations: Show notes provide only the DOI; specific affinities, potency values, antigen targets, and effector-to-target ratios were not captured in this card.
Evidence is primarily cell-based; durable in vivo efficacy, pharmacokinetics of the separate modules, and safety margins are not established here.
Spontaneous chain exchange in circulation or in antigen-negative tissue is a plausible failure mode that would need explicit quantification.
open_questions: What fraction of engager assembly occurs off-target in vivo, measured by antigen-negative tissue exposure versus tumor exposure?
Does the split-prodrug format widen the therapeutic window relative to a matched conventional T cell engager in a head-to-head animal study?
How do the pharmacokinetics and tumor penetration of two separately dosed modules compare with a single molecule?
